framework: China - Interim Measures for Anthropomorphic AI Interactive Services (Order No. 21; promulgated 10 Apr 2026; in force 15 Jul 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Providers must run a security assessment and report to provincial cyberspace authority on launch, major technical change, reaching 1 million registered users or 100,000 monthly active users, or other triggers; assessment focuses on safeguards, training data, extreme-situation response, minors and older adults.
what_is_tested: Security assessment of companion-type AI

framework: China - TC260-PG-20268A Cybersecurity Standard Practice Guide: AI Application Security Guidelines, General (v1.0-202609, TC260 Secretariat, Sep 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: In the verification and validation stage, organisations validate against set reliability, fairness, transparency and explainability metrics; run security tests (manual, automated, cross-validation) by application type: generated-content safeguards; collision and stability for physical devices; explainability, transparency, robustness and backdoor risks for major decisions; protections for minors and special groups. If results fall short, improve (e.g., model tuning) and retest until requirements are met, or redesign.
what_is_tested: Validation metrics; content safety; robustness; backdoor; protections for special groups; retest gate
who_tests: Organisations deploying AI applications; may serve as reference for regulators and third-party testing bodies (Sec. 1)
language_read: Chinese original read in full (PDF from tc260.org.cn via fetch, text extracted); English paraphrase is unofficial translation

framework: China - TC260-PG-20268A Cybersecurity Standard Practice Guide: AI Application Security Guidelines, General (v1.0-202609, TC260 Secretariat, Sep 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: At deployment, use safety guardrails to identify and block illegal content, prevent prompt injection and runaway execution chains; where third-party protection services are used, test and evaluate their security capability and service continuity; perform security checks on hardware, software and third-party tools, fix known vulnerabilities or mitigate, and track vulnerabilities to prevent supply-chain backdoors.
what_is_tested: Guardrail and third-party security capability; vulnerability checks of deployment components
language_read: Chinese original read in full (PDF from tc260.org.cn via fetch, text extracted); English paraphrase is unofficial translation

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Chapter III Sections 1-3 apply from 2 August 2028 for AI systems classified high-risk under Art. 6(1) and Annex I (AI as safety component of, or itself, a regulated product requiring third-party conformity assessment).
what_is_tested: Applicability date of the high-risk requirements for product-embedded systems

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Providers of high-risk systems may exceptionally process special categories of personal data where strictly necessary for bias detection and correction, subject to listed safeguards (no alternative data, access controls, no onward transfer, deletion); paragraph 2 extends this to other operators but creates no obligation to do bias detection.
what_is_tested: Permission to use sensitive data for bias testing

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: The Commission may adopt common specifications by implementing act only if (a) it requested harmonised standards and the request was not accepted, the standards were not delivered on time, insufficiently address fundamental rights, or do not comply with the request, and (b) no reference to covering harmonised standards is published in the OJ or expected within a reasonable period; conformity with common specifications gives a presumption of conformity to the extent covered.
what_is_tested: Fallback technical specifications

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Real-world testing requires a testing plan submitted to the market surveillance authority and approved (tacitly after 30 days unless national law requires authorisation), registration with a unique EU identification number, and a duration of at most six months extendable by six more.
what_is_tested: Authorisation and registration of real-world tests

framework: EU AI Act (Reg. (EU) 2024/1689, as amended by Reg. (EU) 2026/1744)
requirement_paraphrase: Providers must run a post-market monitoring system based on a plan that is part of the technical documentation, actively collecting performance data over the lifetime; the Commission must issue guidance and a template by 2 September 2027.
what_is_tested: Post-deployment performance and compliance monitoring

framework: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1755 (arrangements under Reg. (EU) 2024/1689 Arts 92(6), 101(6))
requirement_paraphrase: When the Commission decides to request access to a GPAI model for an Art. 92 evaluation, the decision sets technical means, conditions and a time limit; access may include APIs, internal access, source code, model weights, hosting infrastructure and the ability to inspect and modify system state; providers must not impose constraints that materially impede the evaluation, may be required to disable logging of the Commission's access, and must grant access without undue delay and within the time limit.
what_is_tested: Regulator-run evaluation of GPAI models (access conditions)
who_tests: Commission / AI Office; appointed independent experts

framework: Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1755 (arrangements under Reg. (EU) 2024/1689 Arts 92(6), 101(6))
requirement_paraphrase: Independent experts evaluating GPAI models for the Commission must be independent of providers (shared ownership, governance, staff or resources and contracts with the provider over at least the prior 12 months are considered), declare interests, and keep confidentiality and information-security protocols; providers may submit reasoned observations on appointed experts; experts are selected by call for expressions of interest (standing list possible), directly from the scientific panel, or under the Financial Regulation.
what_is_tested: Independence and selection of external evaluators of GPAI models

framework: EU AI Act - Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content (Section 1, providers)
requirement_paraphrase: Before placing a generative AI system on the market or putting it into service, and regularly thereafter, signatories test their marking and detection solutions against the Code's requirements under conditions representative of real-world use, using internal benchmarks and industry best practice until recognised methods emerge; they may involve independent experts (notably red teaming for adversarial robustness) or test in AI regulatory sandboxes, and follow up shortcomings.
what_is_tested: Pre-market and periodic testing of AI-content marking and detection

framework: EU AI Act - Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-Generated Content (Section 1, providers)
requirement_paraphrase: Signatories measure detection accuracy (e.g. error rates) on varied samples, including other systems' content and data not used in training, across content length, size, diversity and semantics; they also test robustness to common processing operations (compression, cropping, paraphrasing, translation, print-and-scan) and to adversarial attacks (copying, removal, regeneration, modification of marks) using the same metrics; compliance is demonstrated before market placement and over the lifecycle.
what_is_tested: Reliability and robustness metrics for watermark/marking detection

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: To support post-market monitoring, signatories give an adequate number of independent external evaluators free access to the most capable model version on the market, its chains-of-thought if available, and the least-mitigated corresponding version (unless the model is similarly safe or safer), publish selection criteria, do not train on evaluators' test inputs/outputs without permission, and take no legal or technical retaliation against evaluators who test and publish findings within stated limits.
what_is_tested: Third-party post-market evaluation access and safe harbour

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: Signatories report serious incidents involving their model to the AI Office (and national authorities as applicable) in an initial report within 2 days for serious irreversible critical-infrastructure disruption, 5 days for serious cybersecurity breaches incl. weight exfiltration, 10 days for a death and 15 days for serious health, fundamental-rights, property or environmental harm; intermediate reports at least every four weeks; a final report with root cause analysis within 60 days of resolution; records kept five years.
what_is_tested: Serious incident tracking and reporting for systemic-risk models

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: Signatories obtain assurance that security mitigations meet the Security Goal through independent external security reviews where internal expertise is inadequate, frequent red-teaming of network and physical access management, competitive bug bounties for public-facing endpoints, periodic personnel integrity testing, third-party security reporting channels, endpoint/intrusion detection tools and a security incident response team.
what_is_tested: Security assurance testing of model and infrastructure
who_tests: Signatory provider; independent external security reviewers

framework: EU AI Act - GPAI Code of Practice (Safety and Security chapter)
requirement_paraphrase: Signatories run a full systemic risk assessment and mitigation process at least before placing a model on the market, and give the AI Office unredacted access to the Model Report (evaluation results, mitigations, reasons for proceeding) by the time the model is placed on the market; updates within five business days; delay of up to 15 business days only in good faith with an interim report.
what_is_tested: Pre-market reporting of evaluation results to the regulator

framework: EU harmonised standards work (CEN-CENELEC JTC 21)
requirement_paraphrase: Bias management (18283), dataset quality and governance (18284) and AI conformity assessment framework (18285) are at stage 20 and flagged harmonised.
what_is_tested: Bias, dataset quality metrics, conformity assessment procedures

framework: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2026/2274 on harmonised standards for high-risk AI systems
requirement_paraphrase: The Commission publishes in the Official Journal the reference of EN 18286:2026 'Artificial intelligence - Quality management system for EU AI Act regulatory purposes', developed under standardisation request C(2025) 3871 (point 9 of Annex I, QMS incl. post-market monitoring); conformity with it gives a presumption of conformity with the requirements it covers from publication; the decision enters into force on publication (OJ 14.10.2026).
what_is_tested: Quality management system (incl. verification, test and validation procedures): presumption of conformity
who_tests: Providers apply; notified bodies and authorities rely on presumption

framework: ISO/IEC standards
requirement_paraphrase: Defines methods for measuring the performance of ML models and algorithms on classification tasks; published 13 Oct 2022, 33 pages; stage 90.92; draft ISO/IEC DIS 4213 would widen scope to regression, clustering and recommendation.
what_is_tested: Classification performance metrics

framework: Japan - Guideline for Ensuring Appropriateness of AI R&D and Utilization (decided 19 Dec 2025)
requirement_paraphrase: Operators are to identify and evaluate misuse risks (cyberattacks, fraud) and apply current techniques to reduce inappropriate outputs and malfunction.
what_is_tested: Misuse risk evaluation; output quality

framework: Japan - Digital Agency DS-920 Guideline for Japanese Government's Procurements and Utilizations of Generative AI, v2.0 (decided 12 Jun 2026; in force 1 Sep 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Before releasing a generative AI system, the ministry's planners are to create input/output test scenarios based on its purpose and functions, test inputs and outputs, and confirm stable operation and expected quality. Illustrative methods: checking domain-prohibited outputs, inappropriate generation and social bias, conformity with procurement specifications, and diverse/independent internal and external testing such as red teaming.
what_is_tested: Input/output behaviour, stable operation, output quality, bias, prohibited outputs, specification conformity (red teaming as an example method)
who_tests: Planners in ministries/agencies; vendors/providers may verify data per contract; citizens may take part for public-facing systems
language_read: English provisional translation (Digital Agency) checked against Japanese original

framework: Japan - Digital Agency DS-920 Guideline for Japanese Government's Procurements and Utilizations of Generative AI, v2.0 (decided 12 Jun 2026; in force 1 Sep 2026)
requirement_paraphrase: Each ministry's Chief AI Officer (CAIO), with planners, shall conduct use-case risk assessments and determine the risk level (including whether likely high-risk), referring to the High-Risk AI Project Finder (Appendix 1); likely high-risk cases are reported to the Advanced AI Utilization Advisory Board; the CAIO makes the final determination.
what_is_tested: Use-case risk classification of generative AI (high-risk judgement)
who_tests: CAIO with planners; Advanced AI Utilization Advisory Board advises
language_read: English provisional translation (Digital Agency) checked against Japanese original
